As volumes rise, legislatures are responding. CivicPlus counts more than 20 state and federal measures in play this year, several of which give agencies new ways to say no. California’s, signed in September, declares that AI systems are not “members of the public,” though people may still use AI “at an ordinary human volume and frequency.” A stalled Pennsylvania bill would let agencies deny requests they “reasonably suspect” were generated by a script or AI. Wagenseller doesn’t think that’s the answer. The real choice, she says, is funding agencies to keep up or making the system less free, fast, and open—“and you’re giving up something for both.”

Arguably the most aggressive action yet has been in Indiana, where Allen County officials described a growing trend in “suspiciously non-human” requests for years of purchase orders, eating up to 20 hours a week of staff time, as reported by the Journal Gazette. A state law that passed without a single dissenting vote and took effect July 1 lets agencies charge out-of-state requesters, prioritize residents, and deny requests they suspect are aimed at data scraping or phishing.

Neighboring Adams County went further. In March, it banned commercial use of its records, including resale. The county still hands over the documents, though; a notice of the ban is attached, but there are few means to enforce it. Requests had jumped from about one a week to as many as 10, often in a single burst; since the state law took effect, they’ve settled at one to five. County attorney Clayton Lengerich says the new rules don’t affect “any individual requester’s ability to keep their local municipality accountable,” only requests that “someone’s going to throw into an AI generator for some sales analysis.”

Fielding FOIA requests is expensive, and someone has to pay. Congress tried to put the responsibility on business in 1986, amending FOIA to let agencies charge commercial requesters more, but the rules were so riddled with exceptions that this rarely happens. “It costs more for the agencies to collect the fees than it’s worth in fees, and so they just don’t,” says Kwoka, the Ohio State law professor. She estimates that agencies recoup less than 5% of their costs from commercial requesters; at the FDA in one year she studied, it was $328,000 against $33.6 million spent.

Kwoka has long argued for “affirmative disclosure,” or proactively posting the information that gets asked for most. She points to the EPA, which put property contamination records online after commercial buyers had requested them one address at a time for years. A handful of states have adopted portals, such as California’s Open FI$Cal, that regularly publish high-level spending data. But this doesn’t include the full contracts that sales-tech firms often request, which reveal expiration dates, termination clauses, and service commitments.

Startups like Pursuit and Starbridge say they’d welcome this approach, and they seem confident their business model could survive if the data became freely available. “The best request is one that no one has to file because the data is already out there,” says Vichich. But publishing isn’t free, and commercial requesters also aren’t raising their hands to fund the fix.

As states negotiate reforms, the biggest risk is that rules built to limit bulk AI requests or sales-tech crawlers will land on everyone else: out-of-state reporters, academic researchers, immigration lawyers. Meanwhile, the requests keep increasing. “It’s something we’re going to have to hold our nose and continue doing,” says Rowe, the small-town Vermont clerk. “The alternative sets a dangerous precedent for a person being able to hold government accountable.”

items.title: What a Shopping Editor Is Buying From Net-A-Porter’s Black Friday Sale
items.description: If there’s one Black Friday sale Cut editors always look forward to (and spend the most money on), it’s the Net-A-Porter one. Designer fashion sales aren’t always worth the money — who cares about saving 10 percent when the original price is over $1,000, you k
items.author: Hanna Flanagan
paragraphs: If there’s one Black Friday sale Cut editors always look forward to (and spend the most money on), it’s the Net-A-Porter one. Designer fashion sales aren’t always worth the money — who cares about saving 10 percent when the original price is over $1,000, you know? — but Net-A-Porter’s Black Friday sale is the exception. It’s the retailer’s biggest sale of the year, featuring up to 50 percent off (!) coveted brands like Khaite, Magda Butrym, Agolde, Nour Hammour, Rohé, and more.

There’s a whopping 246 sale pages to scroll through, and you kind of have to hunt (since the pieces with the steepest discounts are usually only available in a few sizes) but that’s where we come in. Below, the best Net-A-Porter Black Friday deals on outerwear, denim, knitwear, dresses, and accessories, according to Cut editors who’ve spent way too much of their free time shopping the sale.
For every other deal, head over to our list of the best Black Friday deals.
The Best Net-A-Porter Outerwear Deals

‘Tis the season to buy all the outerwear your heart desires (which is a lot, if you’re me). Luckily, so many leather jackets, trench coats, heavy wool coats, and even faux fur styles are on sale at Net-A-Porter.
The Best Net-A-Porter Denim Deals
Ah, my favorite category! Save on a wide variety of cuts and washes from Agolde and Frame, plus everyone’s favorite Khaite jeans.
The Best Net-A-Porter Knitwear Deals

There’s no such thing as too many sweaters, in my opinion. The best deals include a sporty, jersey-inspired polo by JW Anderson, a lightweight cashmere sweater by Loulou De Saison, and a festive option by Leset.
The Best Net-A-Porter Dress Deals

The dress section is a mix of formal, seasonally-appropriate styles that are perfect for those who have winter weddings on the calendar, as well as casual daytime dresses you can store in your closet now and pull out on the first nice day of spring.
The Best Net-A-Porter Accessory Deals

From totes and shoulder bags to scarfs, hats, and snoods that will keep you warm this winter, the accessories section has so many gems that are worth shopping. I have my eyes on this Gigi Burris cap that’s 60 percent off.

items.author: Hanna Flanagan
paragraphs: Happy (almost) Thanksgiving break to all. You’re so close to slamming that laptop shut for the long holiday weekend … you can do it! I will unfortunately not be slamming my laptop shut because it’s also almost Cyber Weekend. But luckily for you, that means myself and my fellow Cut editors are going to be sharing all the best Black Friday deals you won’t want to miss. We’ve been working overtime for weeks, searching high and low for the best early Black Friday deals across all categories — from beauty and fashion to home and tech.
Read on for the best deals from Amazon, Sephora, Levi’s, Walmart, and more. Some sales aren’t live quite yet, but check back here throughout the week to take advantage of them when they start.
Updated on November 25, 2026: Updated prices and checked stock for all products.
Stock up on essentials or splurge on luxury beauty
The Best Black Friday Beauty Deals
Bezos never skips a sales event, which is great news for those of us who like to save money on K-beauty and everyday essentials, like UGGs and Bose headphones.

Sephora’s annual sitewide sale may be over, but the beauty retailer is still offering special markdowns during Cyber Weekend. Get up to 50 percent off all weekend, plus earn 4x rewards points on fragrance with code CYBERSCENT.
Get up to 50 percent off over 500 products from brands such as Clinique, Sol de Janeiro, MAC, and more during Ulta’s Black Friday sale.
The K-beauty skin-care brand behind our beauty writer Carol Lee’s favorite skin-barrier cream is up to 45 percent off on Amazon.
Omnilux is having its biggest sale ever, offering $80 off LED devices and deals on bundles.
Another beauty-device brand running a major sale event? CurrentBody. Through December 9, get 20 percent off LED masks and other beauty devices from CurrentBody.
The beauty brand is offering 25 percent across categories, plus an additional 30 percent off and a free Crème de You when you spend $100 or more.
Take 20 percent off everything site wide at Haus Labs, including the editor-loved foundation and concealer, from November 24 to December 1.
Take 20 percent off Laneige skin care products and 25 percent off the brand’s viral lip products through November 30.
Get up to 65 percent off sleep accessories and silk hair scrunchies.
Get 25 percent off site wide at Ouai through December 1, and from November 27 to December 1, get a free four-pack of air fresheners with any purchase.
The namesake beauty brand of Dua Lipa’s makeup artist, Katie Jane Hughes, is offering 20 percent off site wide this week.

Through November 30, take 20 percent off everything (including bundles) sitewide at Summer Fridays. And from November 27 to November 30, the brand is also offering a gift with purchase: Receive a complimentary Cherry Lip Butter Balm when you spend $100 or more.
Therabody’s biggest sale of the year is here. Save on so many of the brand’s best-selling devices, including the Theragun and the TheraFace Depuffing Wand.
Starting on November 27, get 30 percent off everything site wide at Dr. Jart+, including the brand’s beauty-editor-approved face masks.
Paula’s Choice is offering 30 percent off sitewide, plus free shipping when you spend $35 or more, through December 1.
Want to stock up on holiday candles? Shop Nest’s sitewide 25 percent off sale through November 30, plus get free gifts with purchase when you spend $200 or more.
The Best Black Friday Fashion Deals
In need of denim? You won’t want to miss Levi’s Black Friday sale. The brand is offering 40 percent off sitewide, plus free shipping.
Take 25 percent off everything site wide at Reformation, including holiday party dresses, cozy sweaters, outerwear, and accessories.
Alo Yoga’s 30 percent off sitewide sale is on! Save on best sellers and our favorite loungewear.
If you’ve been eyeing one of DeMellier’s gorgeous handbags, now is the time to splurge. Use our exclusive discount code (THECUT20) at checkout to get 20 percent off. I highly recommend the Stockholm.
Ring Concierge is offering 30 percent off everything sitewide (including wedding bands) through December 1.
Through November 30, take 30 percent off sitewide on cashmere clothing, accessories, and more.

One of The Cut editors’ new favorite brands for workout clothes and athleisure, Oner, is offering up to 50 percent right now. Save on tanks, leggings, sports bras, and more for the gym, as well as flared pants and sweat sets for lounging.
Affordable bag brand The Horse is offering 25 percent off their 100 percent leather handbags, shoulder bags, and totes through November 30.
Take up to 60 percent off at Rowie The Label through November 30.
The New York-based brand that prioritizes using natural fibers is offering 20 percent off site wide.
The Best Black Friday Home Deals
If you need a new mattress, you’re in luck: Avocado Green Mattress is offering up to 20 percent off sitewide through December 7.
Save on organic bedding, bath products, and loungewear, plus kitchen décor and mattresses, during Coyuchi’s 25 percent off sale.
Ettitude’s sateen and waffle weaves are 30 percent off, and the luxurious made-in-Peru line is 15 percent off.
The luxury lifestyle brand is offering 20 percent off sitewide through November 30 (some exclusions apply).

You can always find pricey tech items (such as laptops, TVs, and iPads) majorly marked down during Walmart’s Black Friday sale — and this year is no exception. Don’t forget to check out the fashion deals while you’re at it.
Get 25 percent off site wide, plus up to 40 percent off bundles, during Brooklinen’s Cyber Weekend sale.
Boll & Branch has several different promotions happening during Cyber Weekend, like 30 percent off bedding bundles, steep discounts on throw blankets, and up to 50 percent off select styles.
Okay, so Cybex is not technically a home brand, but the Cut-favorite stroller brand is a having a Black Friday sale that’s too good to gatekeep.

items.title: Your Daily Horoscope by Madame Clairevoyant: November 25, 2026
items.description: The sun and Pluto (in Sagittarius and Aquarius, respectively) give you extra strength and influence today. You might be tempted to use these powers to get what you want, without regard for anyone else’s needs. Making selfish decisions might get results in the
items.author: Claire Comstock-Gay
paragraphs: The sun and Pluto (in Sagittarius and Aquarius, respectively) give you extra strength and influence today. You might be tempted to use these powers to get what you want, without regard for anyone else’s needs. Making selfish decisions might get results in the short term, but it’ll ultimately damage your relationships. So take extra care to show consideration for others today.

Today, you might feel you can’t spare the time or energy to help anyone else. In an ideal world, you’d love to lend a hand, but right now you’re just too busy. Still, consider that you might be overestimating what other people need from you. Chances are, they don’t actually want you to drop everything so you can focus on solving their problems. What they really want is a quick favor, maybe a kind word. Small gestures will make a big difference right now, so make them where you can.

You sometimes feel like nobody ever takes your advice. They ask for it, promising to give your words some serious thought — but too often they end up doing what they want, not what you advised. You’ve begun to wonder lately whether you’d be better off keeping your thoughts to yourself. Today, ignore that instinct. People are much more likely to actually do what you recommend right now, so if a friend asks for your thoughts, tell them what you really think. You can make a real difference.

You know your friends very well. There are often times when you can predict exactly what they’ll say in certain situations. As much as you hate to admit it, sometimes that bores you; you don’t enjoy walking into a conversation already knowing how they’ll unfold. But today, the people in your life could surprise you. They might have a new or interesting perspective to share, or their behavior might run counter to precedent — so ask for their thoughts rather than assume how they’ll respond. You’ll be glad you did.

You try to keep your expectations modest. You know that nobody gets everything they want exactly when they want it. But remind yourself that there’s a difference between setting reasonable goals and settling for less than you deserve. If you’ve been feeling unhappy lately, you don’t have to shrug and make the best of things. You’re allowed to want more. Today could be your chance to start making moves to change your life for the better.

Today, tap into your charisma: You’ll be able to get along with just about anyone right now. Just be careful not to put so much energy into winning people over that you save nothing for yourself. As good as it feels to be well-liked, you don’t need everyone to admire you or approve of your choices. If you’re excited about a new project, don’t wait to get started until everyone you’ve ever met is on board. You don’t need permission to get moving.

Sometimes, the problems in your life are too complicated to be fixed in a day — or at all. But other times, things aren’t nearly as difficult as you make them out to be. Today, operate from the assumption that your ordinary efforts can and will make a difference. You don’t need a grand plan that will address everything you’ve ever been unhappy with. Right now, just focus on solving one small issue at a time.

You’re a confident person, and there are days when you worry your own self-assurance might make other people feel bad about themselves. Maybe the brighter you shine, the more others will fade into the background. You might tell yourself the right thing to do is to dim your light, this way nobody else feels inadequate. But today, the last thing you should do is hold back. The people who love you want you to use your gifts. Don’t let other people’s insecurities get in your way.

There’s power in being willing to walk away from a situation that’s not working for you. You try to make it clear to others that if something’s making you unhappy, you’re perfectly willing to shut it down or put it aside. But today, don’t be too eager to quit. Not all difficulty is a sign that things have gone wrong. Sometimes, persevering through hard times is the only way to get somewhere truly great in the end.
Sagittarius Daily Horoscope

As much as you’ll want to do everything your way today, that’s going to be impossible — especially if you’re trying to collaborate with anyone else. Other people have their own ideas about how things should be done, and no amount of pressure will make them fall in line. If you want their support, you’ll have to make some allowances for their needs right now. Consider this a learning opportunity: Your way isn’t always the right one, so keep an open mind and you might learn something useful.

When you see other people making brave stands for what they believe in, or taking dramatic leaps toward their goals, you admire their courage — and you wonder whether you should be moving through the world with equal boldness. But right now, at least, it’s probably better not to do anything particularly flashy or attention-grabbing — grand gestures are likely to be useless at best, and counterproductive at worst. For the time being, focus on taking advantage of the small opportunities to live your values. You might not get much attention for it, but you’ll be making a real difference.

You’re not one to pry into other people’s business. You assume that if they want you to know something, they’ll tell you when they’re ready. But today, your laid-back and patient approach might only make people think you don’t care about what they have to say. They’ll need more encouragement right now if they’re going to share anything meaningful with you, so ask questions and make it clear that you’re interested in the answers. You might be surprised by how much people will reveal.

Today, refuse to get drawn into pointless arguments or caught up in issues you don’t really care about. You might feel it’s cowardly to walk away from a fight or that you have a responsibility to set the record straight if someone says something untrue. But there are times when it’s better to step away than to get involved. Don’t get distracted from your goals right now. There’s no shame in saving your energy for what actually matters.

items.title: The Best Gifts For Your Mani-Obsessed Friends, According To Top Nail Artists
items.description: 22 Gifts That’ll Make Any Nail Lover’s Day
items.author: Iman Balagam
paragraphs: 22 Gifts That’ll Make Any Nail Lover’s Day
Experts share their favorite gifts for the manicure enthusiasts in your life.

Gift-giving can be stressful, especially when your loved ones aren’t exactly sending you neatly organized wish lists divided by price point (my sisters). Thankfully, shopping for someone with a particular passion — like nails — can make things a little easier.

Whether they’re curing their own nails at home with a UV lamp, recreating Hailey Bieber’s latest mani design at the salon every two weeks, or spending a small fortune on nail art without batting an eye, there’s no shortage of options for these friends. Because even the smallest upgrades to their nail routine can feel like a major treat.

To help narrow things down, Bustle polled top manicurists for their favorite nail-centric products to gift. Think reparative treatments for the friend who’s trying to recover from years of biting their nails, cuticle oils that won’t leave their fingers feeling greasy, and hand creams they’ll want to proudly display on their nightstand. And, of course, you can’t go wrong with gifting a new polish shade for their collection.
Below are the best gifts your mani-obsessed loved ones will actually be excited to unwrap.

A hand cream is always a safe bet, particularly during the colder months. Manicurist Vikki Swan recommends this L’Occitane formula, which contains 20% shea butter to nourish dry skin. “It’s a luxurious yet practical gift that complements any manicure routine,” she says.

For the friend who prefers the naked nail look, Swan adores this nourishing polish from Manucurist. “I love how this treatment combines nail care with a beautiful, translucent pink tint and glossy finish,” she says. Designed to nourish and strengthen natural nails, it can be used on both fingers and toes without a base coat, top coat, or UV/LED lamp.
3For The Seasonal Nail Enthusiast

If you’re shopping for someone who swears by a classic holiday manicure, manicurist Viktoriia Voloshyna loves this rich burgundy shade from Gelcare. She calls it her “go-to winter red,” noting that it looks polished on almost every skin tone. “It works for any style, from short natural nails to long ones, and it looks elegant on its own without any nail art,” she says.
4The Handbag Hydration Hero

Cuticle oil is one of those little luxuries your nail-obsessed friend will actually use. Manicurist Elle Gerstein calls this Essie option the perfect stocking stuffer. “I always tell my clients that cuticle oil is a daily essential, especially during the winter,” she says. “I love the roller applicator because you can keep it in your handbag and use it throughout the day.”
5For The Friend Who Loves Options

Gerstein is also a fan of Dazzle Dry’s mini polish collections, particularly this festive set. “The colors are sophisticated, festive, and a little edgy,” she says. “I love gifting mini collections because they encourage people to experiment with colors they might not normally gravitate toward without committing to a full-size bottle.”

Cold-weather feet deserve a little TLC, too. Manicurist Olivia de Montagnac swears by this pedicure kit, which includes everything you need for at-home foot maintenance. “We are not neglecting our feet this winter,” she says. “The callus remover is my all-time favorite, and I like that the exfoliating pads are disposable.”

De Montagnac also recommends this holiday trio from Celisse, featuring three shades that are basically guaranteed to earn a spot in anyone’s polish rotation. “Everything from Celisse is thoughtfully designed and curated,” she says. And the velvet packaging is just one more reason it deserves a spot under the tree.

For a gift that goes beyond the usual nail-care staples, de Montagnac recommends this buttery balm from Summer Fridays. The luxe formula delivers a hefty dose of hydration anywhere from hands to heels. “I use it on my hands, but I also love using it on my legs and feet for a massage,” she says. “Vanilla smells amazing, but Pistachio is my favorite!”

Hand sanitizer may not scream exciting gift, but this set makes the everyday essential feel a little more luxe. Manicurist Marisa Carmichael loves the formulas, which cleanse while keeping hands moisturized. “These are my favorite sanitizers. The scents are gorgeous and not overpowering, and they have a moisturizing serum that leaves hands soft and clean.” Think of it as K-beauty for your hands.
10A Five-Star Cuticle Treatment

If your friend likes her nail care with a side of luxury, Carmichael recommends this cuticle cream. “It feels so elegant and has a really fresh scent,” she says. She's also a fan of its hydrating formula, which nourishes cuticles without leaving behind a greasy residue.
11For Nails In Their Recovery Era

For the friend whose nails have seen better days, Carmichael recommends this bond-repair treatment. “It’s a liquid that penetrates the nail plate and bonds to make nails stronger,” she explains. Even better, it can be worn underneath nail polish, so they don't have to sacrifice their regular mani routine while nursing their nails back to health.

A good body oil is always appreciated, and manicurist Marielle Co says this one is a standout. “Every time I’ve used this product on a client, they rave about it,” she says. “Not only does it smell amazing, but it leaves the skin with a beautiful glow without feeling greasy. It is so nourishing and hydrating. I love that it can be used all over the body, especially on the hands and cuticles.”
13For The Nail-Care Overachiever

Some manicure devotees take their nail health routine very seriously. For these friends, Co recommends adding a strengthening treatment to the mix. “Our nails rely on keratin, so keeping them strong and hydrated is key,” she says. “I always tell my clients that nail health starts with taking care of the natural nail underneath the polish. Strengthening treatments can help improve resilience and reduce breakage — especially if you're trying to avoid those dreaded broken nails.”
14A Paris Fashion Week-Approved Mani

Co first discovered Manucurist backstage at Paris Fashion Week and has been a fan ever since. Known for its vegan, plant-based formulas and more conscious approach to nail care, the brand makes some of her favorite manicure essentials. “I love having a few clean, easy-to-use essentials on hand, and this kit covers three things I think are important: hydration, color, and overall nail health,” she says. “It’s perfect for someone who loves keeping their nails looking polished while still prioritizing the health of their natural nails.”
15For The Nail Art Chameleon

Press-on nails are the ultimate gift for the friend who's rocking a different design every time you see them. Co loves this brand for its range of options across skin tones, shapes, lengths, and designs. “It’s a great way to experiment with different nail looks without committing to a salon appointment,” she says. “There's something for just about everyone's personal style.”
16A Personalized Mani Upgrade

Manicurist Sonya Belakhlef loves this cuticle pen for its luxe feel and customizable, monogrammed pouch. It's also at the top of their own holiday shopping list. “I personally am gifting my clients these pens this year!”
17The Unexpected Nail-Care Essential

For the friend who spends a lot of time behind the wheel, Belakhlef recommends these treatment-boosting gloves. They're a thoughtful alternative to yet another bottle of nail polish — especially for someone whose collection is already overflowing. “I love using these gloves in the car for sun protection,” they say.
18The Ultimate Hand-Care Splurge

If they aren’t messing around with their hand care routine, Belakhlef suggests going all out with this red and near-infrared light therapy glove. Think of it as the gift of 10 minutes of mandatory, phone-free self-care.
A good hand serum should feel as lovely as it works. Belakhlef recommends Sidia for its beautiful scents and textures, and particularly enjoys incorporating its serum into their routine.

Cuticle oil might seem like a simple gift, but it's one they'll actually put to use. Manicurist Sandra Wei recommends looking for a formula with nourishing ingredients like jojoba oil and vitamin E to help ward off dryness and hangnails. “It’s especially beneficial for those who regularly get gel manicures, as daily cuticle care helps keep the skin surrounding the nails soft and well-maintained,” she says.
21Beauty Sleep For Your Hands

For a more indulgent at-home treatment, Wei recommends overnight moisturizing gloves. “I recommend applying a nourishing hand cream and cuticle oil before putting on soft cotton gloves at bedtime to help retain moisture and keep the skin around the nails soft and hydrated,” she says. It's a simple way to turn an everyday hand-care routine into a relaxing at-home spa ritual.
22The Good-Hands Guarantee

Wei is also a big believer in keeping a good hand cream within reach, especially during the colder months. She recommends looking for formulas with moisturizing ingredients like shea butter, glycerin, or ceramides to help protect against seasonal dryness. “This is especially important during the colder months, when the skin around the nails tends to become dry and rough. A good hand cream makes a wonderful holiday gift because it encourages a convenient moment of everyday self-care.”
